findings.message: 19.L SPEC DEPTH says a seeding ticket cites each entry unit its seeds need and never copies unit text into a seed or into its own ticket, because a copy goes stale at the unit's next hardening. This ticket's Scope in has two blocks, 'Carry this complete kill-worker-stop contract verbatim:' and 'Carry this complete kill-failure-suppression contract verbatim:', and each reproduces the unit's full Owner/Records/Observable/Tests bullets. Its Plan contract already cites 19.P3.kill-worker-stop and 19.P3.kill-failure-suppression, so the renderer injects that text anyway. The copies duplicate it and will diverge from the plan the next time either unit is hardened.
findings.paved_road: Delete both verbatim contract blocks from Scope in. Point the implementer to the cited entry units 19.P3.kill-worker-stop and 19.P3.kill-failure-suppression in the Plan contract as the governing text, and keep only ticket-specific instructions such as edges, starts, fence floors and closure greps.

findings.message: Scope in says 'Carry every own-entry Owner, Records, Observable and Tests bullet verbatim' into the implementing seeds. 19.L forbids copying unit text into a seed. Each seed already cites its own entry unit (19.I, 19.P3.<stem>, section 20), and the renderer resolves that citation verbatim, so a copied body is a stale duplicate. It also inflates every seed's render. The successor phase3-continue-12 is told to carry the same instruction forward, so the violation would continue down the chain.
findings.paved_road: Replace the 'carry verbatim' instruction with one that has each seed cite its own entry unit through its Plan contract and add only seed-specific prose: edges, fence, earned closure paths and the Verification command. Have tests/test_seeded_phase3_11.py pin the exact citations instead of copied contract text. Have phase3-continue-12 carry the cite-don't-copy rule forward instead of the verbatim-carry rule.
